observations.text: Selection, mechanical, at be28ba3 (git log -1 --format=%H => be28ba3f8a16fbe11b6b13b4ca546aeadb71b42b; git status --porcelain => empty). No project test-impact selector tool exists: ls scripts/ gives eip-lanes.sh, examine-foundry, slack-record.sh, test-in-lima.sh, test-vm-setup.sh and the only xtask subcommands are ci, smoke, check-arch, openapi (grep of xtask/src/main.rs). Selection is therefore the touched-file to declared-verification mapping of the packet: foundry-core/src/lib.rs + tests/project_key.rs + tests/project_name.rs => cargo test -p foundry-core; migrations/0035 + tests/project_key_db_rule.rs => cargo test -p foundry-store --test project_key_db_rule; xtask/src/check_arch.rs => cargo xtask check-arch; foundry-app/src/projects.rs + the four acceptance step/feature/runner files => cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --release --test acceptance (default lane, no tag); all of them => cargo xtask smoke. Absent selector tooling is recorded here, not substituted by memory.

Reused host-owned native results, cited at their own revision, inputs unchanged. At 644131a (source byte-identical to be28ba3 except crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_fix_hide_unreachable_boards.rs, confirmed by git show --stat be28ba3 naming that single file): cargo xtask smoke printed xtask smoke :: all gates green; cargo test -p foundry-store --test project_key_db_rule 2 passed; the default acceptance lane cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --release --test acceptance reported 110 features, 1904 scenarios, 1901 passed, 3 failed, 16051 steps, 3 failed, exit via panic at tests/acceptance.rs:412 (log /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-canzan-foundry/ae6f0864-8ca5-43d5-b970-fb78c37ae831/scratchpad/pkl-lane.log). Of the 3 failures, 1 was the fix-hide-unreachable-boards rail helper, repaired in be28ba3 (tag then 2/2, smoke green, log .../pkl-fix.log), and 2 were release-version-footer reading Foundry v0.18.2 unknown from a stale 2026-11-14 foundry-app build-script output in the VM target dir, 3/3 after cargo clean --release -p foundry-app. foundry-core, foundry-store and xtask bytes are identical between 644131a and be28ba3, so the core, store-parity and check-arch results carry to the reviewed commit; the acceptance lane inputs changed, so the lane is re-executed below rather than reused.

Concurrent replica start-up with migration 0035 is safe, judged against the code, not the prose. crates/foundry-store/src/lib.rs:230 Store::migrate acquires MIGRATION_LOCK_ID through acquire_migration_lock (lib.rs:4101) which polls pg_try_advisory_lock and holds no snapshot between tries, then applies the pending set and releases with pg_advisory_unlock on every path, so two replicas booting at once serialize and the second finds 0035 already recorded and skips it. 0035 carries no -- no-transaction marker (grep: none), so the drop loop, the ADD CONSTRAINT and the self-check are one transaction: an interrupted or crashed apply rolls back and leaves the 0001 CHECK in force, and the session-scoped advisory lock dies with the connection. Both catalog reads are pinned to projects::regclass, so pg_get_constraintdef can no longer take AccessShareLock on another schema projects and the 40P01 cycle against a sibling AccessExclusiveLock is removed; the lane below applies 0035 concurrently in roughly 1900 per-scenario schemas with no deadlock. The widening is monotone, so an old 2-6 replica serving beside a new one can offer no key the widened CHECK refuses. Residual, named not measured and not introduced by this change: ADD CONSTRAINT takes AccessExclusiveLock on projects and validates its rows, and no lock_timeout is set, so a long open transaction on projects would queue that lock and stall project reads of already-serving replicas for its duration; every prior migration in this repository has the same shape. ADR-001 Consequences call the lock brief and the revalidation safe, which the small-table case supports but does not establish for an arbitrarily long-lived transaction.

Implementation and design quality, object_oriented paradigm, per changed unit. (1) crates/foundry-core/src/lib.rs: the bound has one owner, PROJECT_KEY_MIN_LETTERS and PROJECT_KEY_MAX_LETTERS, read by the length arm and interpolated by the one Display, so the refusal sentence exists textually once; grep of crates/*/src for "Project key finds exactly two lines, lib.rs:102 (the Display) and projects.rs:729 (the already-in-use 409 sentence, a different refusal). ProjectKeyError keeps its three arms as domain diagnosis, the inner field of ProjectKey stays private and try_new stays the only construction point, so the widening changes a bound and no structure. The byte-length arm before the ASCII arm admits exactly the character-based rule, because every accepted key is ASCII; only which arm refuses a non-ASCII key differs, and both render one sentence. (2) crates/foundry-app/src/projects.rs: key_error_message is deleted and the arm renders err.to_string() like the name arm beside it; the unused import is removed, so no second decider of the sentence remains. project_create.html:5 renders that message as

, which is what the oracle step reads, so the assertion is not vacuous. (3) xtask/src/check_arch.rs: the clause reuses OneSourceRule and scan_one_source with no new scanner; scan_one_source (check_arch.rs:5757) fails loudly on a missing or unreadable crates tree and names file:line, so it cannot pass vacuously. The copy_prefix is a prefix match, so a differently worded or line-split copy escapes it; that residual is exactly the gate scope the acceptance row already records. (4) migrations/0035: finds the shipped unnamed CHECK by definition, never by name, and edits no shipped migration; its apply-time self-check cannot currently fail, since the drop loop removes every key_prefix CHECK except the named one, so it is a guard against a future edit of that loop rather than an observation. No anemic domain entity, no domain decision in an application script, no new primitive obsession.

Oracle completeness against the original Request, change the max length of the project key to <=10: every declared behaviour has an executable stimulus and assertions I inspected. Ten-letter accept and its rendering (us-07 Scenario A ten-letter key creates the project and is shown in full, asserting the redirect, the stored row, the board header key and the landing card key); eleven and twelve letters, one letter, empty, lower case, digit, hyphen, space, underscore, accented and Japanese keys refused with 422 and the whole-rule sentence, plus no row under the typed key or a tidied-up variant (the step counts projects by candidate key and by name); two-letter preservation; issue keys PLATFORMOP-1 and PLATFORMOP-10 with exact board listing and a per-prefix absence sweep to highest+3 and a cross-project key sweep read from the projects table; L1/L2/L4 as generated core properties whose expected verdict is restated from the rule, never read back from try_new; L3 as an executed domain-against-database parity probe on a real Postgres reading each verdict separately; L6 as a preservation probe that seeds at both ends of the earlier rule under the staged 0034 set and compares rows across the widening; L7 through the real gate CLI over a planted copy carrying ProjectKeyError::WrongLength.to_string(), with the unplanted copy as the control. No zero-assertion, tautological, mock-dominated, circular or always-green test in the diff; no production object is mocked. Uncovered and correctly out of oracle scope: the dashboard-card layout of a ten-letter key (Y7, a stylesheet question) and the dev-deploy apply of 0035, which remains a completion obligation nobody has observed.

diagnostic: ACCEPTED at be28ba3. The Request, change the max length of the project key to <=10, is delivered and its immutable oracle covers it. Implementation: one owner for the bound (PROJECT_KEY_MIN_LETTERS/MAX_LETTERS in foundry-core), one refusal sentence that interpolates it, the web handler restates nothing (key_error_message deleted, err.to_string() rendered into project_create.html class="error", which is exactly what the oracle step reads), a new migration 0035 that finds the shipped unnamed CHECK by definition and never edits 0001, and one more clause of the existing one-source gate with no new scanner. grep of crates/*/src for the sentence prefix finds the Display alone beside the unrelated already-in-use 409 sentence. Oracle completeness: every declared behaviour has an executable stimulus and real assertions - ten-letter accept with board and card rendering, 13 refused-key rows asserting 422, the whole-rule sentence and no row under the typed or tidied key, two-letter preservation, PLATFORMOP-1 and PLATFORMOP-10 with exact board listing and cross-project sweeps, L1/L2/L4 as generated core properties whose expected verdict is restated from the rule, L3 as an executed real-Postgres parity probe reading each verdict separately, L6 as a seeded-before-the-widening preservation probe, L7 through the real gate CLI over a planted copy of the shipped sentence with the unplanted control. No testing-theater pattern, no mocked production object, no softened fixture or narrowed input in the diff; the only widened generator (project_name.rs fallback address) gained its own checkpoint. Concurrent replica start-up is safe: Store::migrate serialises replicas on the polled MIGRATION_LOCK_ID advisory lock, 0035 is one transaction so an interrupted apply leaves the 2-6 CHECK in force, the catalog reads are pinned to projects::regclass so the 40P01 cycle is removed, the widening is monotone, and my lane applied 0035 concurrently in ~1900 per-scenario schemas with no deadlock; the residual AccessExclusiveLock queueing behind a long transaction is named, unmeasured and not introduced here. Evidence: my own run of the default acceptance lane at this commit is green on every touched feature (us-07 196 steps, one-source 12 steps, hidden boards 17 steps, migration-apply 29 steps) and incomplete elsewhere, its 119 failures all being the single unmet prerequisite CARGO_BIN_EXE_foundry is unset in boot/CLI steps that never read the key rule; the host results at 644131a (smoke green, store parity 2 passed, lane 1901/1904 with all 3 failures explained and the one source change re-run 2/2 with green smoke at be28ba3) are reused with provenance for the unchanged inputs. Two findings are retained, neither blocking this phase: owner oracle, the rail-helper repair in another feature support needs an owner-side record (substance verified - sidebar.html wraps the word in a label span, the new helper reads the same anchor text from the parsed page, and the breakage comes from 2d473dc, not from this change); owner implementation, three statements of the superseded 2-6 bound are still in the tree, one of them in the very document foundry-core cites as the home of invariant I-P3. Open completion obligation nobody has observed: the dev deploy applying 0035 at start-up. typesafe: unavailable (client exit 3, TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent), so every judgment here is local and evidence-backed.
